## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`status()` cuts revisions to 7 characters, while the docstring says it uses the same identifier as `history()`, which uses 12. Fix this so the running status matches the history and completion output.

## Changes
This PR adds `status(revision, attempt)` and `attempt_label(attempt)` to `app/display.py`, which produce a "Running: <revision> (attempt N)" line. It also adds tests for both functions.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/display.py:14 — correctness — Shorten status revisions to 12 characters like history — For `REVISION = "0123456789abcdef…"`, `status()` prints `Running: 0123456`, but `history()` and `completed()` print `0123456789ab` because `revision[:7]` differs from their `revision[:12]`. This contradicts the docstring "using the same identifier as history." — Operators cannot match a running deployment's identifier to its history or completion line by exact text. — Fix: Use `revision[:12]` or a shared helper with `history`/`completed`, and extend `test_running_status_contains_attempt` to assert the full string, because its `startswith`/`endswith` checks cannot detect the length.
